index.title: AstroTurboMaxiSolver · Telescope finder for your phone
index.description: A free telescope finder for your phone. It reads the stars with the camera to know where your telescope points, and guides you to your target, even under a city sky and offline.
index.ogDescription: Reads the stars with your phone's camera to know where your telescope points, and guides you to your target.
index.ldDescription: A telescope finder for your phone: plate solving with the camera, sensor fusion and guidance to your target.
index.subtitle: Because AstroTurbo<wbr />Maxi<wbr />Solver<wbr />Mega<wbr />Finder<wbr />Pro<wbr />Plus was too long.
index.tagline: Push-to for any telescope, with just your phone. No encoders, no mount to change: it reads the stars to know where your telescope points, and guides you to your target.
index.facts: Free · Open source · Works offline · Web app
index.photoAlt: A phone running the app, held on a Dobsonian telescope's tube, with the round puck remote beside the eyepiece

features.title: What it does
features.follows: Move the telescope and the phone's sensors move the map with it. Every plate solve from the camera fine-tunes the position.
features.knows: The camera looks up, spots the stars and works out where your telescope points. Sensor fusion and plate solving, running right in your browser, even with no signal.
features.takes: Pick a target, follow the arrows, and there it is in the rings. Then in your eyepiece.
features.targets: Messier, Caldwell, NGC and IC objects, planets and double stars, with a list of the best in the sky right now. Plus your own lists and an observing log.
features.oldPhone: Old phone in a drawer? Put it on the telescope as the finder, and use another phone to see and control it.
features.puck: Or use AstroTurboMaxiPuck, our remote firmware for the Waveshare 1.75″ round display. Or combine them: a phone as the finder, the puck to aim, and a tablet to choose targets and plan your lists. You decide.
features.city: Tested under Bortle 8 and 9 city skies, the brightest there are. If it finds the stars there, it finds them anywhere.
features.data: Your log, lists and kit are stored on your phone. Sync them between your devices through your own Google Drive, if you like. Never on our servers: we don't have any.
features.free: Free to use, and open source under the GNU GPL. Anyone can see how it works, check it and improve it: the code is on GitHub.

how.title: How it works
how.step1: Fix your phone to the telescope, with its camera looking at the sky.
how.step2: Align once: centre a bright star in the eyepiece and tap.
how.step3: Pick a target, follow the arrows, and enjoy the view.
how.note: Best on Android with Chrome. It works on iPhone with Safari too, with a few limits. Install it from the app to use it full screen.
how.warning: Never point your telescope or your phone's camera at the Sun. Seriously.

faq.title: Questions you may have
faq.internetQuestion: Do I need internet at the telescope?
faq.internetAnswer: No. Open it once at home, and it works offline in the field.
faq.telescopeQuestion: Will it work with my telescope?
faq.telescopeAnswer: If you can fix a phone to it, yes. The phone's camera does the work, not the telescope's.
faq.costAnswer: Nothing. No ads, and no account needed.

about.title: About this project
about.story: AstroTurboMaxiSolver started as a personal project, a tool just for me. I built it quickly in my free time with vibe coding, and it's the first project I've made this way, so expect some things to fail. I find it useful at the telescope, so I wanted to share it with other amateur astronomers.
about.licence: It's free software, under the GNU General Public License version 3. The source code is on GitHub.
about.disclaimer: It's provided as is, without any warranty. It's experimental, not production software, and it may never be.

puck.title: AstroTurboMaxiPuck · A round hand remote for AstroTurboMaxiSolver
puck.description: Free, open source firmware that turns a Waveshare 1.75″ round display into a hand remote for AstroTurboMaxiSolver: the sky map, guidance and your lists, by the eyepiece.
puck.githubLabel: The puck's source code on GitHub
puck.subtitle: Small, round, and it glows in the dark.
puck.tagline: A hand remote for AstroTurboMaxiSolver, on a round 1.75″ display. It shows the app's sky map and guides you to your target, so the phone can stay where it is.
puck.facts: Free · Open source · Wi-Fi, no server · ESP32-S3
puck.photoAlt: The puck's round screen in red night mode: the reticle's rings, nearby objects, and the Alt, Az and field of view along the edge

features.title: What it does
features.map: The phone's sky map, with the reticle and arrows to your target. Alt, Az and the field of view run along the edge.
features.solve: Tap the reticle and the phone plate solves, as if you had tapped it there.
features.lists: Step to the next or previous target, open any of your lists, and align on a bright star, all from the puck's menu.
features.night: Night mode turns it full red, in step with the phone. Its brightness is set on the puck.
features.planetarium: Speaking Meade LX200 over Wi-Fi, it shows Stellarium or SkySafari where your telescope points. A GoTo from them becomes your target.
features.link: It joins your Wi-Fi or your phone's hotspot, or makes its own network. Scan its QR code from the app and they are linked, with no server.

setups.title: Combine it your way
setups.intro: The puck is a remote for a phone or tablet. Where the telescope points always comes from the phone on the telescope.
setups.one: One phone and the puck: the phone on the telescope finds where it points, and the puck guides you from the eyepiece.
setups.two: Two phones and the puck: a phone on the telescope as the finder, a phone or tablet to choose targets and plan your lists, and the puck to aim.
setups.note: The puck links to the phone or tablet, never to the finder: the finder reaches it through them.
setups.photoAlt: A Dobsonian telescope from the side: a phone on its tube, and the puck's round screen beside the eyepiece
setups.caption: The puck by the eyepiece, the phone on the tube.

needs.title: What you need
needs.board: A Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75: a round 1.75″ touch screen with Wi-Fi.
needs.cable: A USB-C cable, to install the firmware and power the puck.
needs.computer: A computer with Chrome or Edge, to install it.

install.title: Install it
install.step1: Install Espressif's ESP-IDF tools, for example with its extension for VS Code.
install.step2: Download the firmware's source code from GitHub.
install.step3: Connect the board by USB, then build and install it: idf.py build and idf.py -p COMx flash.
install.note: The firmware's README has the details, and what to do if the board isn't detected.
install.warning: Work in progress: so far tested on a single board.
install.browser: Connect the board to a computer by USB, open this page in Chrome or Edge, and press Install.
install.unsupported: This browser can't install it: open this page on a computer, in Chrome or Edge.
install.notAllowed: Installing needs this page over https.
install.erase: Updating? Don't erase the board when asked: it keeps its Wi-Fi networks and sky catalogue.
install.link: Then, on the puck, join a Wi-Fi network with its QR code. In the app, open Remote, Puck, and scan the code the puck shows.

privacy.title: Privacy policy · AstroTurboMaxiSolver
privacy.description: What AstroTurboMaxiSolver keeps, where, and what it sends to whom. In short: your data stays on your devices.
privacy.heading: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: In short: your data stays on your devices. There are no accounts, no ads, no analytics and no cookies.
privacy.who: AstroTurboMaxiSolver is a free, non-commercial personal project, run by one amateur astronomer. Contact: astroturbomaxisolver@gmail.com.
privacy.device: Your settings, location, alignment, lists, observing log and equipment are saved in your browser's storage on your device. They are not sent to us: we have no server that could receive them. Removing the app, or clearing the site's data in your browser, deletes them.
privacy.camera: Camera: used to find the stars and work out where your telescope points. The pictures are processed on your device and are neither kept nor sent anywhere.
privacy.motion: Motion sensors: used on your device to move the sky map with your telescope.
privacy.location: Location: used on your device to show the sky from where you are. The app asks for each of these only when you first use something that needs it, and you can say no.
privacy.sentTitle: What is sent, and to whom
privacy.forecast: Weather forecast: to show clouds and seeing, the app sends your location, rounded to 0.1° (about 10 km), to Open-Meteo. Nothing else is sent with it.
privacy.hosting: Hosting: the site is served by Cloudflare, which, like any web host, sees your IP address and the pages requested.
privacy.twoPhones: Two phones: when you link two phones, they talk directly to each other over your local network. Nothing goes through a server. If you turn on "Sync with the linked phone" on both, your lists, log and equipment are copied between them.
privacy.driveIntro: If you choose to connect Google Drive, to keep your devices in sync:
privacy.driveSignIn: You sign in through Google. Google's sign-in page sets its own cookies, under Google's privacy policy.
privacy.driveFolder: The app asks only for access to its own hidden folder in your Drive (the drive.appdata permission). It can't see, read or change any of your other files.
privacy.driveData: Your lists, observing log and equipment are saved there, in your own Drive, and read back by your other devices. They never pass through a server of ours. The access Google gives the app is kept only in your device's memory, and lasts an hour.
privacy.driveDelete: You can disconnect at any time in Settings. To delete the saved data, open Google Drive → Settings → Manage apps → AstroTurboMaxiSolver → Delete hidden app data. You can also remove the app's access at myaccount.google.com/permissions.
privacy.googlePolicy: AstroTurboMaxiSolver's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. The data is used only to sync your own devices, is never shared with anyone, and is never used for advertising.
privacy.children: The app collects no personal data from anyone, children included.
privacy.changes: If this policy changes, the new version is published here, with its date.
